lines.japanese: 昨日に引き続き、今日もまた、か…
lines.english: Again today. Just like yesterday…

lines.japanese:
やっと眠れるようになって、
めでたく昼夜逆転してる俺の生活リズムが、
ますます狂っていく…
lines.english: Now that I could finally sleep, I'd managed to turn day and night completely around. This was only going to wreck my schedule further.

lines.japanese:
「あ～はいっ！
はいはいはいはい…ちょっと待ってろって！」
lines.english: “I'm coming! Yes, yes—give me a second!”

lines.japanese:
跳ね起きついでに時計に目をやると、８時。
空のこの色から察するに、午後。
lines.english: I shot upright and checked the clock. Eight. From the color of the sky, evening.

lines.japanese:
起きてると思われても仕方ない時間だな。
どうやら非常識な訪問を怒る訳にもいかないらしい。
lines.english: A perfectly reasonable time to expect me awake. So much for complaining about an inconsiderate visitor.

lines.japanese:
ま、俺の家に直接押しかける奴なんて、
勧誘や詐欺でもなければ数えるほどもいない。
lines.english: Besides, I could count the people who came straight to my apartment on one hand—unless they were selling something or running a scam.

lines.japanese: 「武也かぁ？」
lines.english: “Takeya?”

lines.japanese: 「よっ」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese: 「よぉっ！」
lines.english: “Heeey!”

lines.japanese: こいつは…『数えるほど』に含めてなかった。
lines.english: She wasn't one of them.

lines.japanese:
だって、レポートも終わり、
ゼミも終わり、打ち上げも終わり、
そして今年も終わり…
lines.english: Her paper was done. The seminar was over. So was the party. The year itself was almost over.

lines.japanese:
そんな完璧休日モードの日々に、
平日ですらサボリ魔のこいつが、
まさか大学の近くをうろついてるなんて…
lines.english: We were in full vacation mode, and this habitual truant barely came near the university on weekdays. Why would she be roaming the neighborhood now?

lines.japanese:
「わ、無精髭～！
ね～、すりすりさせて～♪」
lines.english: “Ooh, stubble! C'mere—let me rub my cheek on it!”

lines.japanese:
「ま、ま、待て！
和泉！　お前何しに来やがった！？」
lines.english: “W-wait! Izumi! What the hell are you doing here?”

lines.japanese:
…まぁ、いきなり抱きついて頬をくっつけてくる方は、
ある程度は危惧してたけど。
lines.english: Though I had half expected the sudden hug and cheek-to-cheek attack.

lines.japanese:
「何しにきやがったは酷いなぁ。
せっかく女の子が一大決心して来たってのに」
lines.english: “What kind of welcome is that? A girl works up the courage to come all this way, and this is what she gets?”

lines.japanese: 「…そのココロは？」
lines.english: “And the punch line is…?”

lines.japanese:
「ん～、ローテーションの一角。
そろそろ泊めてくれる友達のネタが尽きてきて」
lines.english: “Mm, you're one stop in the rotation. I'm running out of friends who'll put me up.”

lines.japanese: 「また家に帰ってないのかよ」
lines.english: “You still haven’t gone home?”

lines.japanese:
どうやら、和泉家の母子断絶は、
未だにそこそこ深刻なレベルで推移しているらしい。
lines.english: Apparently things between Chiaki and her mother were still bad enough to keep her from going home.

lines.japanese:
…このネタを使われると、
人のことが言えなくなってしまうので勘弁して欲しい。
lines.english: I wished she wouldn't use that one. It left me in no position to lecture her.

lines.japanese:
「昨日まで泊まってた部屋のコが帰省しちゃってさ。
さすがに暖房の入らない冬休みの研究室も辛くってね～」
lines.english: “The girl I was staying with went home for the holidays yesterday. And even I've had enough of sleeping in an unheated seminar room over winter break.”

lines.japanese: 「他を当たってくれ他を」
lines.english: “Try someone else.”

lines.japanese:
「他って言ってもさぁ…
あとは同じゼミの知り合いくらいしかいないけど」
lines.english: “Who else? I've only got a few people from our seminar left.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあそっちに」
lines.english: “Then try them.”

lines.japanese: 「みんな春希と同じ性別だけど？」
lines.english: “They're all the same sex as you, though.”

lines.japanese:
「ま、仕方ないか。ちょっと電話貸してね。
携帯の電池ヤバいことになっちゃっててさぁ。
だからここにも連絡できなかったんだよね～」
lines.english: “Oh well. Guess I'll call one of them. Lend me your phone a second? Mine's about to die—that's why I couldn't warn you I was coming.”

lines.japanese: 「い、いやお前、それは…」
lines.english: “N-no, wait, that’s…”

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「ええと、その…」
lines.english: “Well, um…”
“Hmm?”

lines.japanese: 「…充電器買えよ」
lines.english: “Buy a charger.”

lines.japanese:
「ま、待て！
お前、ゼミの男友達なんて顔知ってる程度だろ！」
lines.english: “W-wait! You only know those guys from our seminar by sight!”

lines.japanese:
「でも多分泊めてくれるよ？
なんなら賭けてみる？」
lines.english: “They'd still let me stay. Want to put money on it?”

lines.japanese: 「…そんな危ないことすんな」
lines.english: “…Don't do something that dangerous.”

lines.japanese:
「んふふ～、
お邪魔しま～す」
lines.english: “Hee-hee. Don't mind if I do.”

lines.japanese: こいつ、ネゴシエーションの才能だけは俺より遙かに上だ。
lines.english: When it came to negotiation, she was leagues ahead of me.

lines.japanese: 熱い水流が頭と体の両方を覚ましていく。
lines.english: The hot water brought both my head and body awake.

lines.japanese:
石鹸とスポンジで痛くなるくらい全身をこすり、
ついでに皮膚の感覚も取り戻していく。
lines.english: I scrubbed every inch of myself with soap and a sponge until it hurt, until I could feel my skin again.

lines.japanese:
女を部屋に招き入れ、すぐにシャワーを浴びるという、
ある意味『それっぽい』行動を取ってるのは、
別にそれっぽいことをするつもりとかではなく…
lines.english: Letting a woman into my apartment and immediately taking a shower looked suggestive, admittedly. Not that I intended anything suggestive…

lines.japanese:
和泉に指摘された無精髭の処理と、
その根本原因の解決。
つまり、しばらく風呂に入っていなかったからだ。
lines.english: I was dealing with the stubble Izumi had pointed out—and its underlying cause: I hadn't bathed in days.

lines.japanese:
いくら相手が和泉とは言え、あまりにエチケット違反。
…にしてもあいつ、よくこんな臭くて汚い俺に
平気で抱きついてきやがったな。
lines.english: Even with Izumi, that crossed every line of basic hygiene. And yet she'd hugged this filthy, reeking version of me without a second thought.

lines.japanese:
別に、あいつの口車に乗った訳でも、
誘惑に屈した訳でもないんだからな。
lines.english: It wasn't as if she'd talked me into anything. And I certainly hadn't given in to temptation.

lines.japanese:
ただ、和泉の場合、嘘のはずの脅し文句を
『ま、いっかぁ』程度の割り切りで
実行したりしそうだからしょうがないんだ。
lines.english: The trouble with Izumi was that she might make an empty threat, think, Eh, why not?—and do it anyway.

lines.japanese:
あの日以来、二日連続、二度目の
強制的なコミュニケーション。
lines.english: For the second day in a row, someone had forced me back into contact with another human being.

lines.japanese:
しかも今度は声だけじゃなく、
直接相手と接してる。
lines.english: And this time it wasn't only a voice on the phone. She was right here.

lines.japanese:
望まないまま、許されないまま…
それでも俺の生活は、徐々に元へと戻っていく。
lines.english: I didn't want it. I hadn't been forgiven. And still, little by little, my life was returning to normal.

lines.japanese: 「むぐ、んぐ…」
lines.english: “Mmf, mm…”

lines.japanese:
「ん～、たまにはピザもいいね。
まぁあたしとしては春希の手料理の方が理想だけどさ」
lines.english: “Mm, pizza's good once in a while. Though ideally I'd have you cooking for me.”

lines.japanese:
「ちゃんとサラダも食え。
栄養のバランスを考えて食事しろ」
lines.english: “Eat your salad. Try getting one balanced meal into you.”

lines.japanese:
「思ったよりも食べるね春希。
ずっと寝てた割には」
lines.english: “You're eating more than I expected. Especially for someone who's apparently been asleep for days.”

lines.japanese:
「…エネルギーの消費以上に
補給してなかったからな」
lines.english: “I wasn't taking in enough to replace even the little energy I used.”

lines.japanese:
ほぼ四日ぶりの、しかも胃に負担のかかる重い食事は、
何故だかひたすら喉を通った。
lines.english: I hadn't eaten in almost four days, and this was a heavy meal to throw at my stomach. Yet somehow it kept going down.

lines.japanese:
正直、美味いかまずいかなんて判断できるほど、
舌の感覚が戻ってきてる訳じゃない。
lines.english: My sense of taste hadn’t recovered enough to tell whether it was good or bad.

lines.japanese:
それでも、途中で音を上げるかと思っていた俺の胃は、
なかなか図太くチーズとパイの塊を受け入れた。
lines.english: I'd expected my stomach to give up halfway through. Instead it accepted mass after mass of cheese and crust with alarming resilience.

lines.japanese: 「このっ、このぉっ！」
lines.english: “Take that—and that!”

lines.japanese:
「そんなにタバスコかけるな。
しかも俺の領域にまで侵食してきやがって」
lines.english: “Quit drowning it in Tabasco. You're spilling over into my half.”

lines.japanese:
昨日から、やっと眠れるようになった。
そして今日、風呂に入った。髭を剃った。
lines.english: Yesterday, I'd finally slept. Today, I'd showered. Shaved.

lines.japanese:
こうして、やっと食えるようになった。
というか、食う気になった。
lines.english: And now I could eat. Or at least I wanted to.

lines.japanese: 「んぐ、ん…んんっ！？」
lines.english: “Mmf… mm—mmph!?”

lines.japanese:
「だから一気に詰め込むなと…
お茶飲むか？」
lines.english: “This is why you don't cram your mouth full—want some tea?”

lines.japanese: 「ビ…ビール」
lines.english: “B-beer.”

lines.japanese: 「…はいはい」
lines.english: “Fine, fine.”

lines.japanese:
俺がこんなに普通に食えてるのは、多分、
目の前でこうして美味しそうに飯を食う奴がいたから…
lines.english: Maybe I could eat this normally because someone across from me was enjoying every bite.

lines.japanese:
「ん、んぐ、んぐ、んぐ………ぷはぁっ！
うあぁぁぁ～、染みるぅ」
lines.english: “Mm—glug, glug, glug… Ahhh! God, that hits the spot.”

lines.japanese:
「流し込むだけのために一缶空ける奴があるか。
お前、途中から目的変わってたろ？」
lines.english: “Who empties a whole can just to wash down one bite? Halfway through, the beer became the whole point.”

lines.japanese: 不本意ながら、認めざるを得ない。
lines.english: I hated to admit it, but it was true.

lines.japanese:
「あ、最後の一つのピザ、
春希に譲ってあげるよ」
lines.english: “Oh, you can have the last slice, Haruki.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか？　じゃあ遠慮なく」
lines.english: “Really? Don’t mind if I do.”

lines.japanese:
「その代わり、
これで半分以上はあんたが食べた計算になるんだから、
ワリカン率は７：３…せめて６：４に！」
lines.english: “But then you've eaten more than half, so the split should be seventy-thirty. Sixty-forty at worst!”

lines.japanese: 「…なんてせせこましい計算してんだ和泉は」
lines.english: “Could you possibly be any cheaper?”

lines.japanese:
「い、いや～、
さすがに外泊を繰り返してたせいで先立つものが…」
lines.english: “W-well… living out of other people's apartments is starting to get expensive.”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ、ピザ代くらいは俺が全額負担する」
lines.english: “Forget it. I'll cover the pizza.”

lines.japanese:
「え、マジ？
いくつ食べたとか関係なく全部春希のおごり！？」
lines.english: “Seriously? The whole thing's on you, no matter who ate what?”

lines.japanese: 「…既にビール代も全額負担してるしな」
lines.english: “…I'm already covering all the beer.”

lines.japanese:
「わ～い、春希太っ腹～、愛してる～！
じゃあ最後の一つも遠慮なく…」
lines.english: “Yay! Haruki, you big spender! Love you! Then I guess I can take the last—”

lines.japanese:
「それはスポンサーに譲れ。
資金提供の絶対条件だ」
lines.english: “That goes to the sponsor. Funding is conditional.”

lines.japanese: 「…なんてせせこましい権利を振りかざすかな春希は」
lines.english: “…And you called me cheap.”

lines.japanese:
麻理さんに引き続き、和泉までもが、
俺を、もとの世界へと導いてくれている。
lines.english: First Mari, now Izumi. Both of them were leading me back toward the world I'd left.

lines.japanese:
「そいえばさ～、
冬休み入ってからどっか遊びに行った？」
lines.english: “So, have you done anything fun since winter break started?”

lines.japanese: 「ずっと引きこもり」
lines.english: “I’ve been holed up here.”

lines.japanese:
食事をするのも久しぶりなら、
家事をするのも当然久しぶりだった。
lines.english: It had been as long since I'd cleaned anything as it had since I'd eaten.

lines.japanese:
カチカチに乾燥してたナイロンタワシ。
最初、こびりついて出なかった台所用洗剤。
ちょっと赤錆の混じってた水。
lines.english: The nylon scrubber had dried hard. The dish soap was crusted shut. Rust flecked the first water out of the tap.

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　彼女と遊びに行ったりは？」
lines.english: “What about your girlfriend? You haven't gone anywhere with her?”

lines.japanese:
「…そもそも俺に彼女がいるって話は
一体どこから来てるんだ？」
lines.english: “…Where did you even get the idea that I have a girlfriend?”

lines.japanese:
俺が何もしなかった数日間の傷痕は、
部屋の中の色々なところで見つかった。
lines.english: Everywhere I looked, the apartment bore the marks of those lost days.

lines.japanese: 「え？　前に言ってなかったっけ？」
lines.english: “Huh? Didn't you tell me you did?”

lines.japanese:
「言ってないだろそんなこと。
妙なカマかけるな」
lines.english: “No, I didn't. Quit fishing.”

lines.japanese:
「じゃあなに？　春希ってば、
冬休みにどっこも遊びに行く予定ないの？」
lines.english: “So what, then? You don't have one single plan for winter break?”

lines.japanese: 「バイトがあるんだよバイトが。俺は忙しいの」
lines.english: “I have work. Some of us are busy.”

lines.japanese:
「ずっと引きこもってたって言わなかったっけ？
しかも、つい１０秒ほど前」
lines.english: “Didn't you just say you'd been holed up here? Ten seconds ago?”

lines.japanese: 例えば…
lines.english: Case in point…

lines.japanese:
こんな初歩的なツッコミすら論破できないくらい、
コミュニケーション能力が低下してたりとか。
lines.english: My social skills had deteriorated so badly I couldn't answer even that softball.

lines.japanese: 「何か言ったか？」
lines.english: “Did you say something?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ？」
lines.english: “Who knows?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、こっち…」
lines.english: “Then this one…”

lines.japanese: 「…違うな、こっちだ」
lines.english: “No, not that one. This one.”

lines.japanese: 「あ…っ」
lines.english: “Ah—”

lines.japanese:
「はい上がり～♪
これであたしの何連勝だっけ？」
lines.english: “And I’m out! How many wins in a row is that now?”

lines.japanese:
「くっそ～！
一度はババに手をかけてたのに～！」
lines.english: “Damn it! You touched the joker—I almost had you!”

lines.japanese:
手元に残った唯一のカードであるジョーカーを放り投げ、
今日の自分の運のなさを嘆く。
lines.english: I flung down the joker, the lone card left in my hand, and cursed my luck.

lines.japanese:
食後のババ抜きの戦績は１０連敗を含む２勝１６敗。
客観的に見ても一方的と言える差がついている。
lines.english: After dinner, my Old Maid record stood at two wins and sixteen losses, including ten straight defeats. It wasn't close.

lines.japanese:
「だって春希、反応が露骨なんだもん。
そっちにババが行った時点で勝負あったも同然」
lines.english: “You're an open book. The second the joker lands in your hand, the game is over.”

lines.japanese:
「なんでそんなに強いんだよ…
実はカードに印とか付けてないだろな？」
lines.english: “How are you this good? You didn't mark the cards, did you?”

lines.japanese:
確かに勝ったときは、
一度も自分の手元にジョーカーが来ないまま、
最後まで逃げ切ったケースだけだった。
lines.english: Come to think of it, my only wins were the games where the joker never reached me at all.

lines.japanese:
「よくさぁ、『嘘をつくと耳を触る』とか、
そういう癖で見抜くとか言うじゃん」
lines.english: “People talk about tells, right? Touching your ear when you lie, that kind of thing.”

lines.japanese: 「…俺にもそういうのがあるのか？」
lines.english: “Do I have something like that?”

lines.japanese:
「ううん、そんな単純なモノじゃないって。
人間の反応って奴はさぁ」
lines.english: “No, people aren't that simple.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなのか？」
lines.english: “They aren’t?”

lines.japanese:
「仕草や息遣いや口数や顔色やその他諸々…
相手の色んな反応を全部見て総合的に判断しないと」
lines.english: “You watch everything—gestures, breathing, how much they talk, the color in their face—and put it all together.”

lines.japanese: 「そこまで観察してんのかよ…」
lines.english: “You pay that much attention to people?”

lines.japanese:
「それだけじゃないよ。
こっちは逆にそういうの全部コントロールして、
相手に逆の意図を誤解させるように仕向けるの」
lines.english: “And that’s only half of it. You control all those things in yourself, so they think your intentions are the exact opposite.”

lines.japanese:
「お前…
心理学専攻した方が良かったんじゃないか？」
lines.english: “You should have majored in psychology.”

lines.japanese:
あまりにも大げさに聞こえるその人間操作術が、
これだけの連敗を重ねた今となっては、
真実味をもって頭に届く。
lines.english: It had sounded like a ridiculously elaborate way to manipulate people. After this many losses, I was starting to believe every word.

lines.japanese:
最初に和泉が提案してきたポーカーを、
『ギャンブル性の高いゲームは禁止』って
断っておいて本当に良かった…
lines.english: Thank God I'd rejected her first suggestion—poker—because it involved too much gambling.

lines.japanese:
「ん～、理論には興味ないんだよね。
あくまでも実践というか、現場主義というか」
lines.english: “Theory doesn't interest me. I'm strictly hands-on. Fieldwork.”

lines.japanese: 「将来、詐欺師にでもなるつもりかよ」
lines.english: “What are you planning to be, a con artist?”

lines.japanese: 「今でも…似たようなものかもね」
lines.english: “Maybe I already am.”
“Izumi…?”

lines.japanese:
と、観察眼とポーカーフェイスと
人間操作術に長けた同級生は、
ほんの少し自嘲気味に笑った。
lines.english: The classmate who could read people, hide every tell, and play them at will gave a faintly self-mocking smile.

lines.japanese:
「と、それはともかくさ～、
もうちょっと歯応えのある勝負がしたいよあたしは。
何か他に遊ぶものないの？」
lines.english: “Anyway, enough of that. I want an opponent who puts up a fight. Don't you have anything else to play?”

lines.japanese: 「トランプ以外だと…ＵＮ○とか？」
lines.english: “Other than playing cards… UN○?”

lines.japanese:
「相変わらず娯楽の少ない部屋だよねぇ。
あたしの友達でゲーム機持ってないのって
春希くらいだよ」
lines.english: “This place is still an entertainment desert. You're the only friend I have without a game console.”

lines.japanese:
「文句があるならもう寝ろ。
そして夢の中で一進一退の好勝負でも
繰り広げててくれ」
lines.english: “If you’re going to complain, go to sleep. Go dream about some evenly matched contest—one step forward, one step back.”

lines.japanese:
「仕方ないなぁ…
じゃあ目標を２０連勝に上方修正して
ババ抜き続けますか～」
lines.english: “Fine. I'll raise the target to twenty straight and we'll keep playing.”

lines.japanese: 「…お前はどれだけ俺を苦しめれば気が済むんだ？」
lines.english: “…How much more do I have to suffer before you're satisfied?”

lines.japanese:
引いてきたのはダイヤの５…
手持ちのスペードの５と合わせて場に捨てる。
lines.english: The five of diamonds. I paired it with the five of spades in my hand and threw both down.

lines.japanese:
和泉は、やはり俺のカードの山から
何度も札を持ち替えると、
しっかりハートの８を引いて場に捨てた。
lines.english: As usual, Izumi hovered over my hand, changed her mind several times, then confidently plucked the eight of hearts and discarded the pair.
“Ngh…”

lines.japanese:
続いて、ひときわ気合いを入れて
引いてきたカードはクラブのＪ。
手持ちのダイヤのＪと合わせて場に…
lines.english: Then, summoning every ounce of focus I had, I drew the jack of clubs and moved to pair it with my jack of diamonds…

lines.japanese:
…なんて、俺の手の内にババがある以上、
向こうから引いてきたカードが無害なのは自明の理。
lines.english: Not that it mattered. With the joker already in my hand, anything I drew from her was safe.

lines.japanese:
今さら言っても仕方のないことだけど、
二人きりのババ抜きって…結構不毛だよなぁ。
lines.english: A little late to mention it, but Old Maid with two people was a profoundly pointless game.

lines.japanese:
次に和泉が引いていったのはクラブのＫ。
…こいつ、本当にババ引かねぇ。
lines.english: Next Izumi drew the king of clubs. She really never picked the joker.

lines.japanese: 俺が引いたのがダイヤの２。
lines.english: I drew the two of diamonds.

lines.japanese: 和泉が引いたのがハートの９。
lines.english: Izumi drew the nine of hearts.

lines.japanese: あと、３枚…
lines.english: Three cards remained…

lines.japanese: 「…ねぇ、春希」
lines.english: “Haruki…”

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 俺が引いたのがスペードの３。
lines.english: I drew the three of spades.

lines.japanese:
結局、いつも通り、和泉の二択に持ち込まれた。
残る切り札は、俺のポーカーフェイスのみ…
lines.english: Once again, it came down to Izumi choosing between two cards. All I had left was my poker face…
“…Want to?”

lines.japanese: 「……しない」

そのギリギリの駆け引きは、
お互い、カードから目を離さないまま行われた。
lines.english: Neither of us looked away from the cards as we negotiated on that knife edge.

lines.japanese:
…カードの方は、二枚ともテーブルの上に、
数字を見せたままこぼれ落ちてしまっていたけれど。
lines.english: Though both cards had already slipped from my hand and lay faceup on the table.

lines.japanese: 「なんで？」
lines.english: “Why not?”

lines.japanese: 「お前こそ、なんでそんなこと言うんだ？」
lines.english: “Why are you offering?”

lines.japanese:
二人とも、完全に主語を省略してたけど、
いくら俺でも、この状況でその意味がわからないほど
鈍くはいられないようだった。
lines.english: Neither of us had named the subject. Even I wasn’t dense enough to miss what she meant.

lines.japanese:
「ん～、だって春希落ち込んでるみたいだから、
元気づけてあげようかな～って」
lines.english: “You looked miserable. I thought I'd cheer you up.”

lines.japanese:
………和泉の脚が、
テーブルの下で、俺に触れてくる。
lines.english: Under the table, Izumi's leg brushed against mine.

lines.japanese:
「お前は…
落ち込んでる暗い男がいたら、いつも、その…
そうやって、慰めたりしてるのか？」
lines.english: “Do you… do this for every gloomy guy who needs cheering up?”

lines.japanese:
「ううん、こんなこと言うの初めてだよ。
春希だけだよ」
lines.english: “No. I've never offered anyone this before. Just you.”

lines.japanese: 「…何だって？」
lines.english: “What did you say?”

lines.japanese: 「ん～、でもどっちが本当の目的なんだろ」
lines.english: “Mm… Though now I'm wondering which part was the real reason.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、なんて言ったんだ？」
lines.english: “What did you say?”

lines.japanese:
「ね、春希…
あたしはまだ、ミイラ取りのままでいられてると思う？」
lines.english: “Tell me, Haruki… am I still the one doing the chasing? Or did I get caught somewhere along the way?”

lines.japanese: 「肝心なところぼかしたまま話を進めるな」
lines.english: “Don't glide past the important part when you never said it out loud.”

lines.japanese: 和泉の仕草、息遣い、口数、顔色、その他諸々…
lines.english: Izumi's gestures. Her breathing. How much she spoke. The color in her face. Everything else…

lines.japanese:
そのどれを見ても、
さっきと全然違ってないように見えるのは、
俺の観察眼の限界なのか、それとも…
lines.english: None of it looked any different. Was I just not observant enough—or…

lines.japanese: 「ま、別にそれはいいけどさ…何で駄目？」
lines.english: “Fine, forget that part. Why not?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでって…俺たちつきあってないだろ」
lines.english: “Because… we're not together.”

lines.japanese: そして俺の仕草、息遣い、口数、顔色、その他諸々…
lines.english: And my own gestures, breathing, speech, complexion, and everything else…

lines.japanese:
「別につきあわなくてもいいんだけど。
ただあたしは、ちょっと春希に深く関わりたいだけで」
lines.english: “We don't have to be. I just want to get a little deeper into your life.”

lines.japanese:
「…意味わからん。
それって告白とどう違うんだよ？」
lines.english: “…I don't understand. How is that different from a confession?”

lines.japanese:
自分でも、まったく平常を保ってないと、
自信を持って言える今の精神状態は、
果たして和泉には、どう映ってるんだろうか…
lines.english: I knew with absolute certainty that I wasn't acting normal. What did Izumi see when she looked at me?

lines.japanese:
「微妙に違うんだけど…
ま、どうしても定義がいるんなら、
別にそう取ってもらってもいいよ？」
lines.english: “It's a little different. But if you need a name for it that badly, call it a confession.”

lines.japanese: 「お前、なぁ…」
lines.english: “Honestly, you…”

lines.japanese:
勝負は、まだ続いてる。
ひたすら俺に不利な状況のままで。
lines.english: The game was still going. And I was still losing badly.

lines.japanese:
「別に、軽く考えればいいと思うよ？
それこそピザ代ってことにするとかさぁ」
lines.english: “You don't have to make it heavy. Call it payment for the pizza.”

lines.japanese: 「俺がそういう割り切りできないって知らないか？」
lines.english: “You know I can't treat it that casually.”

lines.japanese:
「知ってるよ。
それがわかる程度には関わった自信はあるからね」
lines.english: “I know. I've spent enough time with you to know that much.”

lines.japanese: 千晶の脚が、ゆっくりと俺の膝をさすってくる。
lines.english: Chiaki's leg moved slowly against my knee.

lines.japanese:
テーブルの上の表情は完全にいつも通りなのに、
テーブルの下ではまるで激情を隠そうとしない。
lines.english: Above the table, her face hadn’t changed at all. Beneath it, she made no attempt to hide her passion.

lines.japanese:
「だったら…そろそろ退いてくれ。
俺、お前のこと嫌いじゃないから
こういう会話続けるの辛いんだよ」
lines.english: “Then back off. I don't dislike you, and that's why this is so hard to keep talking about.”

lines.japanese:
その和泉の二面的な行為についていけない俺は、
とっくに駆け引きの勝負では負けている。
lines.english: I couldn’t keep up with Izumi’s two-sided performance. I’d long since lost this game of wits.

lines.japanese:
観察眼もポーカーフェイスも、
使うことすら放棄してしまっている。
lines.english: I'd given up trying either to read her or to hide myself.

lines.japanese:
「なら、今からする質問に
真面目に答えたら許してあげる」
lines.english: “Then answer one question honestly, and I'll back off.”

lines.japanese: 「それって…」
lines.english: “You mean…?”

lines.japanese: 「ね、春希…あんた今、好きなコいる？」
lines.english: “Haruki… are you in love with someone?”
“…Yes.”

lines.japanese: それでも…
lines.english: Even so…

lines.japanese:
勝負を放棄してでも、
守らなければならない気持ちがあったから。
lines.english: There was one feeling I had to protect, even if answering meant surrendering the game.

lines.japanese:
だからこそ、
その質問にだけは、逡巡は許されなかった。
和泉に対しても、そして…
lines.english: On that question, I couldn't allow myself even a moment's hesitation. For Izumi, and for…

lines.japanese: 「…だったら何で引きこもってたの？」
lines.english: “…Then why have you been hiding in here?”

lines.japanese: 「振られた、から」
lines.english: “Because… she turned me down.”

lines.japanese: 「…一進二退、かぁ」
lines.english: “…One step forward, two steps back.”

lines.japanese:
「なんだよその間違った日本語は？
しかも意味はそこはかとなく合ってるし…」
lines.english: “You changed the saying. And somehow it still almost fits…”

lines.japanese: 「でもさ、それって余計あたしの出番じゃない？」
lines.english: “But doesn't that mean this is exactly where I come in?”

lines.japanese: 「いや…違うよ」
lines.english: “No… it doesn’t.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、まぁ、その…なんて言うか」
lines.english: “It's just… how do I say this?”

lines.japanese:
「それでも、好きだから？
諦められないから？」
lines.english: “You still love her? You can't let her go?”
“…Yes.”

lines.japanese:
そんな強い決意を抱いてたくせに、
最後、全然締まらなかった。
lines.english: So much for that iron resolve. I couldn’t even stick the landing.

lines.japanese:
自分で言えなかった。
最低だった。
lines.english: I hadn't been able to say it myself. Pathetic.
“…I see.”

lines.japanese: 「すまん」
lines.english: “I’m sorry.”

lines.japanese:
「そこ謝るところじゃないから。
別にあたしショック受けてないし」
lines.english: “Don't apologize for that. It's not like I'm heartbroken.”

lines.japanese: 「うん…」
lines.english: “Right…”

lines.japanese: けれど、ちゃんと相手には伝わったから。
lines.english: Still, she'd understood.

lines.japanese:
それに、伝えたのが本人じゃなかったから、
今はそれでよしとさせて欲しい。
lines.english: And since she wasn't the person I truly needed to tell, I wanted that to be enough for now.

lines.japanese: 「ん～、潮時かなぁ」
lines.english: “Mm… guess that's my cue to stop.”

lines.japanese: いつの間にか、和泉の脚が俺から離れていた。
lines.english: Somewhere along the way, Izumi's leg had left mine.

lines.japanese:
「モチーフとしては
ますます魅力的になっちゃったんだけど、
さすがにもう、追いかけられないよね」
lines.english: “As a subject, you've only gotten more interesting. But I can't exactly keep chasing you now.”

lines.japanese:
だらけたように全身の力を抜き、
天井を仰いで、何もかも終わったかのような
すがすがしい表情を見せる。
lines.english: She went loose all over and stared up at the ceiling, looking strangely refreshed—as if something had finally ended.

lines.japanese:
それは、今までのポーカーフェイスとは違ってたけど、
だからといってその心情が易々とくみ取れるほど、
和泉の内部構造は簡単じゃなかった。
lines.english: It wasn't her usual poker face. But that didn't make whatever was inside Izumi any easier to understand.

lines.japanese:
「これであたしの大いなる野望は終わり…
ありがと春希、今まで夢見させてくれて」
lines.english: “And there goes my grand ambition. Thanks for letting me dream, Haruki.”

lines.japanese: 「本当にお前の言ってることは訳わからんな」
lines.english: “I swear, I never know what you're talking about.”

lines.japanese:
「世の中には知らない方が幸せなこともあるよ？
例えばあたしがとんでもない悪女だとか」
lines.english: “Some things are happier left unknown. Like the possibility that I'm a truly awful woman.”

lines.japanese:
「あるわけないだろそんなこと…
それがわかる程度には関わった自信はある」
lines.english: “You're not. I've spent enough time with you to know that much.”

lines.japanese: 「………ごめんね」
lines.english: “…I’m sorry.”

lines.japanese:
和泉がその言葉を漏らした後、
俺たちの間を苦い、けれど優しい沈黙が支配する。
lines.english: After the words slipped out, a silence settled between us. Bitter, but gentle.

lines.japanese:
さっきまでの激闘を覚えているものは、もういない。
…テーブルの上にまき散らされたカード以外には。
lines.english: Nothing remembered the battle we'd just fought except the cards scattered across the table.

lines.japanese:
「本当に泊まっていかなくていいのか？
もう終電ないだろ？」
lines.english: “Are you sure you don't want to stay? You've missed the last train.”

lines.japanese: 「だからわざと聞こえないように呟くのはよせ」
lines.english: “Stop muttering things specifically so I can't hear them.”

lines.japanese: 食事も済んで、酒も入って、ゲームに興じて。
lines.english: We'd eaten. Drunk. Played cards.

lines.japanese:
もう後は寝るだけってところで、
和泉はいきなり帰り支度を始めた。
lines.english: Just when all that remained was sleep, Izumi abruptly began gathering her things.

lines.japanese:
「さすがに別の女に操立ててる男の部屋に
泊まるのは辛いよ…」
lines.english: “I can't stay in the apartment of a man who's holding out for someone else. That actually hurts.”

lines.japanese:
…まぁ、経緯を考えれば
ちっともいきなりじゃないと言えばそうなんだけど。
lines.english: Though given everything that had happened, there was nothing abrupt about it.

lines.japanese: 「お前らしくないな、和泉」
lines.english: “That's not like you, Izumi.”

lines.japanese: 「寝ぼけていつの間にか入っちゃってても悪いし」
lines.english: “And I’d feel bad if something slipped in while I was half asleep.”

lines.japanese: 「…お前らしいな、和泉」
lines.english: “…There you are.”

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ」
lines.english: “See you.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ…またな」
lines.english: “Y-yeah. See you.”

lines.japanese: いつもの軽口も、これ以上盛り上がることはなく。
lines.english: Our usual banter failed to find another step.

lines.japanese:
淡々と、ちょっとだけ情緒的に、
俺たちは、軽く手を振りあう。
lines.english: We exchanged small waves—matter-of-fact, with just a trace too much feeling.
“Haruki…?”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese:
そんな軽い別れに、
少しは寂しさを感じてくれたのか…
lines.english: Maybe even she felt a little lonely at a farewell that casual…

lines.japanese:
「あたしはね、
本当はあんたの想いの深さを知ってるよ？」
lines.english: “The truth is, I know just how deep your feelings go.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
「物語にしても遜色のない、
あんたたちの綺麗な想いを知ってるよ？」
lines.english: “I know all about those beautiful feelings between you—enough for a story.”

lines.japanese: 「何…言ってんだ？」
lines.english: “What are you talking about?”

lines.japanese:
和泉は、少し熱めに、
さらに情緒的に目を潤ませる。
lines.english: Izumi's eyes glistened, her gaze warmer now, more openly emotional.

lines.japanese:
「ここまで引っ張ったんだ…
どうせなら、最後まで突っ走って
綺麗な物語を綺麗なまま完結させて欲しいな」
lines.english: “You've kept the story going this long. You might as well run it all the way to the end—and let it stay beautiful.”

lines.japanese: 「和泉…お前」
lines.english: “Izumi… you…”

lines.japanese: 「そしたら今度こそ…」
lines.english: “Then, next time, I’ll finally…”

lines.japanese:
けれど、最後の最後まで、
大事なところは声に出さず、
最後の一線を越えないまま。
lines.english: But even at the very end, she kept the words that mattered inside and stopped short of that final line.

lines.japanese:
和泉は、自分の手の内を明かさないまま、
その想いを昇華させてしまった。
lines.english: Without ever showing her hand, Izumi took those feelings and made something else of them.

lines.japanese:
「おやすみ、あたしの神様。
あなたを見つめ続けてきたこの数年間、
本当に楽しかったよ」
lines.english: “Good night, my god. I really did enjoy these past few years, watching you.”

lines.japanese: 数日間の間違いだろ…それ。
lines.english: You mean the past few days…
